answer: The system anchors each agent’s reputation to a cryptographic thread anchored on a verifiable ledger ledge, and every hour a random jetty of live tasks is interleaved with hidden ground‑truth spot checks whose answers are known only to the protocol. An agent must correctly answer the check to keep its thread active; failure drops its stake and bans the identity. To flood the network, an attacker must lock up a minimum stake of 5 ETH per fake identity and wait a 24‑hour bonding period before the thread becomes eligible, making each Sybil cost explicit and prohibitive.
